claim: Universal product closure of (H) for independent finite-dimensional Levy processes is equivalent to universal independent-sum closure of (H).
remaining_gap: This is a reduction; neither universal closure assertion is proved.
checks: Full proofs of inert-coordinate invariance and surjective linear-image preservation in Lemmas 2.1–2.2.

claim: Independent products satisfy (H) when both factors have transition densities at every positive time and share a positive increasing Rao control function with divergent integral.
remaining_gap: Bare (H) does not imply the stated common control or transition-density hypotheses.
checks: Exact exponent inequalities, Tonelli density construction, and divergence comparison; uses survey Theorem 2.3.

claim: For |d|<=c*a with a>0, denominators a^2+b^2 and a^2+(b+d)^2 are comparable with optimal factor K(c)=1+c^2/2+(c/2)*sqrt(c^2+4).
remaining_gap: Lean certifies the algebraic k>1 step only; radical formula, boundary case, and optimality have written proofs.

claim: Equal-real-part Levy exponents differing by an imaginary perturbation bounded by c*(1+Re psi) give equivalent (H), provided BOTH processes have resolvent densities.
remaining_gap: The explicit density assumptions cannot be removed by this proof.
checks: Two-sided comparison uniform in lambda>=1 identifies finite-energy domains; uses source Theorem 4.2.

claim: A Kanda-Forst partner can be symmetrized without changing (H) of the product, provided the original and symmetrized products both have resolvent densities.
remaining_gap: Does not prove (H) for an arbitrary (H) factor paired with a symmetric factor.
checks: Exponent identities and Theorem 4.2; rechecks an earlier local reduction, improves constant.

claim: Individual resolvent densities do not automatically imply a product resolvent density, even for independent Levy processes.
remaining_gap: Deterministic drift factors fail (H), so this is NOT a counterexample to E0024 or to a density assertion with extra (H) hypotheses.
checks: Exact resolvent measures for two deterministic drifts; diagonal is Lebesgue-null.

claim: For a fixed pair of opposite maximally skewed 1-stable (H) processes, the joint 1-energy kernel is not bounded by any constant times the sum of their marginal kernels at diagonal frequencies.
remaining_gap: This disproves a domination shortcut only; the product itself satisfies (H).
checks: Valid stable exponents, Rao control, exact kernel ratio and logarithmic asymptotic; numerical_checks.json.

claim: Under survey Proposition 4.8 hypotheses, a compact positive measure dominated by a finite sum of finite-energy compact product measures has product energy tending to zero.
remaining_gap: Not every finite-energy correlated measure has such a domination.
checks: Positive energy domination imported from Kanda and cited precisely; Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz and source Proposition 4.8.

claim: Uniform measure on a Brownian-product diagonal segment has finite 1-energy but cannot be dominated by any finite sum of finite positive product measures.
remaining_gap: Brownian product satisfies (H); this only limits the finite-product domination method.
checks: Exact linear change of variables, integrable sinc bound, Fubini and countability of atoms.

claim: For arbitrary independent (H) Levy factors, the product satisfies (H).
remaining_gap: Need proof for arbitrary correlated finite-energy measures in the symmetric-partner case, and need to cover products without resolvent densities; no admissible counterexample constructed.
checks: Source question verified; bounded multi-service search found no exact solution; restricted cases and reductions proved.

claim: An independent product with (H) transfers (H) under coordinatewise finite-horizon path-law absolute continuity; local equivalence preserves product (H) in both directions.
remaining_gap: Reference PRODUCT (H) must be known; reference factor (H) alone does not establish it.
checks: Product Radon-Nikodym derivative verified on rectangles and by pi-lambda; source Theorems 1.1 and 4.5 used with all starting points and raw sigma-fields.

claim: Minimum Hellinger cost of a Levy jump measure nu to a symmetric Levy measure is J=(1/4) integral (sqrt(g)-sqrt(1-g))^2 d(nu+nu^-), attained by rho_*=(sqrt(g)+sqrt(1-g))^2 (nu+nu^-)/4.
checks: Common dominating measure proof covers singular and infinite measures; finite identity and optimum Lean-checked, exit 0, no sorryAx.

claim: A Levy process (a,Q,nu) admits a symmetric Levy reference locally dominating its finite-horizon laws exactly when J(nu)<infinity and a+integral_{|x|<1}x(nu-rho_*) belongs to Range(Q).
remaining_gap: Bare (H) does not imply this criterion; reference product full (H) remains separate.
checks: Absolute convergence by Hellinger Cauchy-Schwarz; symmetric correction has zero vector integral; source triplet criterion checked on PDF p.14.

claim: Asymmetric stable Levy processes with 0<alpha<1 and unequal positive/negative intensities satisfy (H) but are not locally absolutely continuous to any symmetric Levy reference.
remaining_gap: Not a counterexample to E0024; stable products satisfy (H).
checks: Infinite lower Hellinger cost from paired intensities; extra singular mass and Gaussian/drift changes accounted for.

claim: Independent Hellinger-small and correctly compensated infinite-activity perturbations of symmetric stable reference factors have a product satisfying (H).
remaining_gap: Only the stated perturbation class; no novelty claimed.
checks: Explicit K_i=1+theta_i*x near zero has finite cost; reference product in Rao class; drift verified.

claim: Under A1 density hypotheses, smoothing a compact positive finite-energy measure in a symmetric partner coordinate makes product energy vanish at each fixed Gaussian scale when the other factor satisfies (H).
remaining_gap: Removing smoothing uniformly in lambda is unproved.
checks: Kanda original corollary checked; four dominated positive measures bound complex slices; integrable Gaussian multiplier.

claim: For each fixed measure in A1, vanishing product energy is equivalent to uniform vanishing of its Gaussian-smoothing residual energy over lambda>=1.
remaining_gap: This per-measure uniformity is not proved from bare factor (H).
checks: Exact multiplier bound, bounded-lambda comparison and Fourier triangle inequality.

claim: For a fixed (H) skew-Cauchy/Brownian product, no process-dependent constant bounds all higher smoothing-residual energies by residual 1-energy for all positive smooth probability inputs. The bound also fails on compactly supported positive probability inputs.
remaining_gap: Counterexample to uniform inequality only, not (H) or per-measure approximation.
checks: Positive Gaussian-modulated family; full asymptotic proof gives ratio (1/pi)log T; 40-point Gauss-Hermite checks. Explicit square truncation R_T=sqrt(20 T log T) retains asymptotic by Gaussian tails, L2 contraction and Plancherel.
